messages.text: Kartal hails her mentality after 'dream come true' run to Wuhan Open final

metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."
metadata.content: Sonay Kartal on 'dream come true' Wuhan Open run as British player reaches first WTA 1000 final | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sonay Kartal on 'dream come true' Wuhan Open run as British player reaches first WTA 1000 final Great Britain's Sonay Kartal says mental side of sport "one of my strongest assets" as she prepares for Wuhan Open final against Poland's Maja Chwalinska on Sunday, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am ; Kartal beat Jelena Ostapenko 7-6 7-6 in semi-finals on Saturday Saturday 17 October 2026 18:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open semi-final between Sonay Kartal and Jelena Ostapenko Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets." Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko. The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match. messages.text: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes

metadata.summary: Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot.
metadata.content: Ascot: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes for Gosden team | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ascot: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes for Gosden team Ombudsman reversed the form with last year's winner Calandagan in the latest renewal of the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes at Ascot under William Buick; result was one of three successes on the day for owners Godolphin, who also claimed the QEII and Balmoral Handicap Saturday 17 October 2026 17:06, UK Image: Ombudsman won the Champion Stakes Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot. It was Francis-Henri Graffard's French raider who took home the spoils 12 months ago, but this time around there was a decisive verdict in favour of John and Thady Gosden's home favourite, who obliged as the 5-4 market leader. With the six-strong field heading into the home straight grouped tightly, the stage was set for Ombudsman to demonstrate the blistering turn of foot that has often been a hallmark of his career. When William Buick asked him to quicken, he scorched past eventual third Bay City Roller before seeing off Calandagan to banish Juddmonte International disappointment and prove he is truly one of the best middle-distance horses on the planet. messages.text: Almeraq proves his class in British Champions Sprint

metadata.summary: Almeraq confirmed himself as this season’s star sprinter with a third top-level triumph of the campaign in the Qatar Racing British Champions Sprint Stakes at Ascot.
metadata.content: Ascot: Almeraq proves his class in British Champions Sprint | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ascot: Almeraq proves his class in British Champions Sprint William and Maureen Haggas celebrated further success with their star sprinter Almeraq, who chased down Paborus to strike in the Qatar Racing British Champions Sprint Stakes under Tom Marquand. Saturday 17 October 2026 15:09, UK Image: Tom Marquand and Almeraq enter the winners' enclosure Almeraq confirmed himself as this season’s star sprinter with a third top-level triumph of the campaign in the Qatar Racing British Champions Sprint Stakes at Ascot. After coming out on top in a thrilling Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot, William Haggas' 11-10 favourite bounced back from July Cup disappointment with a blistering display in the Sprint Cup on very soft ground at Haydock. With conditions not as testing this time, the four-year-old - who was involved in a horrific fall at York that ultimately ended Jim Crowley's riding career a little over a year ago - showed all of his class and versatility in the hands of Tom Marquand. He answered every urging from his rider to hit top gear close home and run down Ed Bethell's Paborus for a neck success. Completing a one-three for the Somerville Lodge was Division.
